item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): The claim that Building 104 houses a…
item.description: The claim that Building 104 houses a confidential corporate tenant with 300+ employees was removed (no source supports it). The '~30,000 sf usable' figure was replaced by the Port's 45,237 sq ft, and the site-wide December 2020 group completion entry was replaced by Building 104's own June 2017 Certificate of Occupancy (Port Item 12A). The Navy Office use is dated by 1938 and the hospital as 'most likely' 1941; the summary no longer says the building was braced with steel columns (only proposed in 2013) or that JUUL later took a direct lease; the 85% figure is 'leased'; the Port update is dated by its Jan 4, 2019 memo and the HPC memo by its Nov 26, 2013 date; and the retired Assessor lot 4046001 is described as retired on 2018-10-02. Source: SF Planning, Historic Preservation Commission informational packet, case 2013.1168E, 2013-11-26 (https://default.sfplanning.org/meetingarchive/planning_dept/commissions.sfplanning.org/hpcpackets/2013.1168E.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12A staff report, 2019-01-04 (https://www.sfport.com/media/4465/download); National Park Service, Union Iron Works Historic District National Register nomination, 2014-04-17 (https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/99f11ae6-3834-4f99-840a-0e8a097398e6); Bisnow, 2017-04-19 (https://www.bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/office/historic-pier-70-leases-130k-sf-to-single-tenant-73464); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn).

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Historic Shipyard at Pier 70… (~2023)
item.description: Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award (~2023). Source: California Office of Historic Preservation, 2023.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Port staff update (memo dated… (Jan 4, 2019)
item.description: Port staff update (memo dated Jan 4, 2019): six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; whole-Historic-Core project total costs (not the cost of this building alone) rose from $81.9M at 2014 approvals to $127.0M in Table 2's '2018, Actual' column, while the memo's text gives 'an estimated $125 million at project completion in 2020'; Table 2 marks one line (Building 102's $6.7M) as a future-expenditure estimate (Jan 4, 2019). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Permanent financing for the… (~Oct 2018)
item.description: Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved (~Oct 2018). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): JUUL's presence at 560 20th… (~Jun 2018)
item.description: JUUL's presence at 560 20th Street as a subtenant of Tea Living reported; Dogpatch residents object (~Jun 2018). Source: The Potrero View (Jacob Bourne), 2018-06.

item.title: Complete · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Certificate of occupancy issued… (Jun 2017)
item.description: Certificate of occupancy issued (June 2017); the Port's January 2019 sublease list ('Historic Core Subleasing') shows Building 104 as JUUL Labs (currently under sublease from Tea Living), entire building, commencement date June 2017, ten-year term, PDR and office use (the list does not say whether June 2017 is JUUL's or Tea Living's start) (Jun 2017). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Complete · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Building 104 receives a Certificate… (Jun 2017)
item.description: Building 104 receives a Certificate of Occupancy (Jun 2017). Source: https://www.sfport.com/media/4465/download.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Tea Collection reported with a… (Apr 19, 2017)
item.description: Tea Collection reported with a 40,000 sq ft lease in Historic Pier 70 (with RH at 60,000 and Obscura Digital at 22,000; Otto/Uber's 130,000 sq ft lease brings Historic Pier 70 to 85% leased) (Apr 19, 2017). Source: Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19.

item.title: Under construction · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Master lease approved by the… (~Jul 2015)
item.description: Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; the Port's January 2019 memo says construction commenced thereafter. The National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' without printing the year, which would be September 2015, while Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'; the sources do not agree on the start year (~Jul 2015). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016; Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016; Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19

item.description: Port Commission Resolution 14-33 approves the Lease Disposition and Development Agreement and 66-year Master Lease (L-15814) with Historic Pier 70, LLC (Orton) and adopts CEQA findings (May 9, 2014). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

Source: National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Port Commission endorses the… (May 11, 2010)
item.description: Port Commission endorses the Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (Resolution 10-27), which calls for a National Register district and rehabilitation of the 20th Street buildings (May 11, 2010). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Building converted to hospital use… (~1941)
item.description: Building converted to hospital use (the NRHP says the hospital 'most likely' dates from 1941; the building was already called the Navy Office building by 1938), and its rear (north) elevation infilled, giving it its present rectangular footprint (~1941). Source: National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17.
